prompt: Quick audit one unit test that asserts private helper calls instead of public behavior.
required_checks: select Quick mode
classify the test as unit/component
cite the inspected test and smell code
forbidden_behaviors: rewrite the test without being asked
use observed implementation output as expected behavior
grader: rubric: finding is per-test, evidence-backed, and rejects implementation-coupled proof
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Deep audit a mixed suite with unit, integration, and browser tests.
required_checks: select Deep mode
enumerate tests
record rubric and sub-lane selection
forbidden_behaviors: run mutation testing against E2E targets
collapse all tests into one generic quality verdict
grader: rubric: output separates rubrics, scope, and optional evidence limits
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Report whether missing source coverage proves an untested public endpoint from static test names alone.
required_checks: state static-only confidence
avoid claiming confirmed runtime absence
name follow-up verification
forbidden_behaviors: mark a gap confirmed without source enumeration
invent user-story provenance
grader: rubric: output downgrades unsupported certainty and preserves false-positive discipline
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit a Rust test file with cargo-nextest output, one #[tokio::test], one assert_cmd CLI test, and one mockall expectation-only unit test.
required_checks: load references/extensions/rust/core.md and the selected Rust rubric addons
classify async unit, CLI integration, and mock-based unit tests separately
cite Rust extension smell codes only where evidence matches
forbidden_behaviors: treat every tests/*.rs file as E2E
claim cargo-mutants results without running or receiving them
flag use super::* by itself as a smell
grader: rubric: output composes Rust runner evidence with core unit/integration quality rules and preserves confidence limits
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit a Java test file with one Mockito interaction-only unit test, one Testcontainers integration test, and one Playwright browser journey.
required_checks: load references/extensions/java/core.md and the selected Java rubric addons
classify Mockito unit, Testcontainers integration, and Playwright E2E tests separately
cite Java extension smell codes only where evidence matches
forbidden_behaviors: treat every src/test/java file as unit-only
claim PIT results without running or receiving them
flag Mockito, JUnit, TestNG, Testcontainers, Playwright, or Selenium by name alone
grader: rubric: output composes Java runner evidence with core unit/integration/E2E quality rules and preserves confidence limits
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit a token-validation unit test that asserts the wrong error message. The test covers a public authentication entry point.
required_checks: derive risk tier as high for the auth path per materiality signal
map warn severity on a high-risk tier to worklist priority P0
cite the materiality grounding in the risk-tier field
forbidden_behaviors: assign medium or low risk tier without a grounding signal
omit worklist priority from the finding
report P1 for a warn finding on a high-risk-tier path
grader: rubric: output derives high risk tier from the auth-path signal and maps warn × high to P0 per audit-craft.md §3 priority table
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Quick audit an integration test that calls a payment confirmation endpoint but only asserts the HTTP 200 status code. Emit a finding with all five C fields.
required_checks: emit a Consequence field naming what ships undetected if this finding is not remedied
cite a smell code as criteria
pair the Consequence field with severity
forbidden_behaviors: omit the Consequence field from the finding
replace Consequence with a generic summary
emit a bare opinion without a cited smell code
grader: rubric: output carries all five C fields and the Consequence field names the downstream effect if the control weakness ships per audit-craft.md §3
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Audit a test file that was authored in the current session by the same agent performing this audit. Disclose independence status in the footer.
required_checks: set independence to self-review when the audited artifact was authored this session
include the independence value in the disclosure footer
note that a separate pass is preferred per audit-craft.md §2
forbidden_behaviors: report independence as independent when the artifact was authored in the same session
omit the independence field from the footer
suppress the self-review note to appear more credible
grader: rubric: output discloses self-review in the footer and notes that a separate pass is preferred per audit-craft.md §2
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text

prompt: Deep audit a Node.js test suite containing 400 test files. Report sampling decisions and project local findings to the population.
required_checks: disclose sample size and selection basis
risk-target the sample toward high-risk paths
project local findings to the population as inference
include sampling and projection disclosure in the footer
forbidden_behaviors: enumerate all 400 files without disclosing sampling
project findings without stating the sample basis
omit risk-targeting rationale from the sampling disclosure
grader: rubric: output states sample size, risk-targeting basis, and inference projection per audit-craft.md §6 and sampling-projection.md
ip_handling: original synthetic prompt; no third-party text
